parts.title: My grandmother's letters
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
My grandmother lives in a small village in the mountains, and she does not have a computer or a mobile phone. When I was little, she wrote me a letter every month, and I loved to open the envelope and find a picture or a dried flower inside.

One day, I asked her why she did not just send an email. She smiled and said, "A letter is different. Someone has touched the paper, and you can keep it for a hundred years." I did not understand then, but I do now.

Last summer, I found a box in her attic with letters that her own mother had written to her sixty years earlier. Some of them were about small things, such as the weather or a neighbour's new baby. But reading them, I felt as if I could hear my great-grandmother's voice.

Now I write to my grandmother too, once a month, in my best handwriting. It takes me a long time, but it is a nice change from typing on my phone. And when her answer arrives, I put it in a box, next to the others, because I would like my own children to find it one day.

parts.title: How does a letter travel?
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
When you put a letter in a postbox, it begins a long journey. [1] A van comes to the postbox every afternoon and takes all the letters to the local sorting office.

At the sorting office, the letters are put through a machine. [2] It reads the address in less than a second and sends each letter to the right place.

Then, the letters go on a lorry, a train or sometimes a plane. [3] If your letter is going to a distant country, it may travel on three different kinds of transport.

At the other end, the same thing happens in the opposite order. [4] The letter arrives at a local office, where it is given to a postman or postwoman.

Finally, the post worker walks or cycles through the streets and puts the letter through your friend's door. [5] From start to finish, it may take only two days, or up to two weeks, depending on the distance.
sentences: This is the part of the trip that is the quickest.
The machine is much faster than any human worker.
Nowadays, most mail travels at night, when the roads are empty.
It is hard to believe that so many people are involved.
First, the letter is collected by a worker in a van.
This depends on how far the letter has to go.

gaps.explanation: First, the letter is collected, which follows the sentence about starting a journey and leads to the van coming.
The machine is faster than any human worker and reads the address in a second.
The distance decides the vehicle, and the next sentence says a far country may need three kinds of transport.
Most mail travels at night when the roads are empty, so the letter arrives at a local office in the morning.
It is hard to believe that so many people are involved, and the last sentence gives the total time.

parts.title: Letters or messages?
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Today, most people send messages on their phones [1] of writing letters. Messages are quick and cheap, and you can send one in a few seconds. However, there are things that a letter can do [2] a message cannot. A letter is something that you can hold in your hands and keep in a box. It can be read many years later, [3] a message is often lost when you change your phone. Some people say that writing by hand makes you think [4] carefully about what to say. Of course, a letter is slower, and you must buy a stamp. But [5] you have a friend who lives far away, a letter can be a lovely surprise. Why not try writing one this week? You may be surprised at how good it makes you [6].

gaps.explanation: Instead of writing letters means in the place of them.
Things that a letter can do: a relative pronoun.
A letter lasts, while a message is often lost: contrast.
If you have a friend far away: a condition.
Makes you feel good: a verb after make.

parts.title: A talk about the history of the post
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: bridget
turns.text: Good morning, everyone. Today, I will tell you a little about the history of the post. The first postal service in Britain started in the year fifteen hundred and sixteen. At that time, messages were carried by men on horses. The first stamp in the world was the Penny Black, which appeared in eighteen forty. Before stamps, the person who received the letter had to pay for it, and sometimes, people refused. With the stamp, the sender paid in advance, and the system became much simpler. The Penny Black showed a picture of Queen Victoria, and it was black, as the name says. Soon, other countries copied the idea. Today, more than one hundred billion letters are sent around the world every year. Although many of us now use email, people still love to receive a card or a parcel. The busiest time of the year for postal workers is December, when millions of Christmas cards are delivered in a few weeks.

parts.title: An interview with a postwoman
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Honor, you have been a postwoman for fifteen years. What time does your day start?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: At six in the morning, in the sorting office. We put the letters in order, and then I load my bag and set off by about eight.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How far do you walk every day?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: About twelve kilometres. My phone counts my steps, and some days, I reach twenty thousand. I do not need a gym!

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the best part of the job?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: Meeting people. I know almost everybody on my route, and many of them offer me tea on cold days. One old gentleman gives me a biscuit every Friday.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the worst part?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: Dogs! Most of them are friendly, but one or two do not like uniforms. I have learned to keep a gate between us.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you ever get strange requests?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: Once, a little girl gave me a letter for her grandmother and asked me to deliver it by hand. The grandmother lived next door, so I did, and I received a big hug.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Will you stay in the job until you retire?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: I hope so. The work is hard, but I love being outside, and I feel I do something useful for everyone.
